# PR 247 performance review

Verdict: PASS WITH NOTES at `9b4edcecb50cec1f12ace63060e9a1d762b7be25`. No blocking performance finding. Scope: performance; correctness/security have separate assigned reviewers.

## Cost findings

1. `crates/daemon/src/http/memory_turn.rs:1034-1061`: SETTLE is a deadline on the existing event wait, not a poll, a new task, or a fleet-wide/per-seat timer. The wake is `min(settle, bound)`; working clears the settle and a later idle creates a new deadline. Existing `hold` and admission tasks remain; no additional spawn is introduced. Cost scales with pending held closes/compacts and their events, not every fleet seat on a tick. The settle is a brake (only delays; the bound remains), while deciding turn-end is policy.
2. The same seat-filtered live subscription now accepts `memory.note` as a third event kind. It does not open another subscription or scan the spine. One event-loop exit reaches the single existing proceed/record path. No new repeating work.
3. `grant_note_grace` adds one BTreeMap entry by pane only after a held close succeeds (`closed.is_some()`). It prunes expired entries on a subsequent grant: O(G) retain plus O(log G) insertion, where G is the retained grace entries. Expired entries may remain allocated while no further close lands, but are authorization-inert and are pruned on the next grant; growth is tied to close bursts, not uptime/ticks. `note_grace` performs an O(log G) lookup and one process-start probe only for an unregistered caller attempting memory add with an unexpired matching grace. No sweep is added.
4. Activity traffic decreases. OMP removes one idle HTTP publication per model/tool iteration while preserving the existing working publications at turn_start and final idle at agent_end(false). Copilot removes the intermediate idle AND usually the following working publication because observeActivity already deduplicates unchanged working state. session.idle, abort, fusion_completed, and shutdown still provide its idle paths. No new hook/tick/launch is added. Existing tool-boundary delivery/resend handling is retained, independently of seat.activity.
5. The process-start claim needs one qualification: normal own-live-process probes use macOS proc_pidinfo or Linux /proc in-process, but existing ProcLiveness::proc_start falls back to the already-counted absolute `/bin/ps` probe on an unreadable existing process or conversion failure (`crates/harnesses/src/proc.rs:90-104,286-293`). Thus this is no new launch SITE and no steady-state launch, not an unconditional guarantee of zero launches for every possible grace attempt. The fallback is already counted as `ps.proc-liveness-fallback`, covered by the existing spawn-site sensor. No such fallback appeared in the baseline interval. Existing memory-add persistence launches are unchanged.

Relevant state consumers inspected: idle-nudge candidates require actual Idle (`idle_nudge.rs:90-98`); watchdog fleet activity and PA scope tracking read current Working/Idle; cold-wake bypasses Working (`core/cold_wake.rs:169`); PA digest hides working seats; PA size refresh reads working/previously-working or generation-changed seats (`pa_presence.rs:990-1061`). These consumers need true ongoing work/end-of-work, not tool-boundary false idles. Existing PA working-seat refresh may now correctly remain eligible across tool boundaries; its cadence is unchanged. This is source analysis, not a claim that the post-deploy fleet path has already been exercised.

## Live pre-deploy receipts

Command, in the detached review worktree:
`date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ && pij-rs --json ping && just spawn-rate --seconds 20 && date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ && pij-rs --json ping`
Exit 0. Window: 2026-11-19T00:37:28Z through 00:37:48Z; sampler duration 20.0 s. Both pings: daemon PID 23167, live commit 577a6c7a13 (NOT the candidate).

| Exact daemon counter | Before | After | Delta / 20 s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| total | 591 | 592 | 0.05/s |
| git.pa-watchdog-common-dir | 28 | 29 | 0.05/s |
| all other by_op counters | unchanged | unchanged | 0/s |

Whole-machine sampler: total_new_per_s 186.2; sampled_per_s 164.7; polls 137563. Attributed lower bounds: gone-before-seen 111.7/s, other 52.9/s, pij-rs daemon 0.0/s. Observed daemon children pij-rs 0.0/s; statusline runs 0.1/s. The sampler's displayed daemon 0.0/s is a lower bound/rounding, not a contradiction of the exact one-launch delta.

Subsequent resource snapshot: `/bin/ps -p 23167 -o pid=,%cpu=,rss=,etime=,command=` exited 0 and returned PID 23167, CPU 18.2%, RSS 165712 KiB, elapsed 36:28, `/Users/jordanknight/.npm-global/bin/pij-rs daemon`. CPU is ps's reported snapshot, not an interval CPU benchmark.

## Verification and limits

`git rev-parse HEAD` in `/Users/jordanknight/pi-hacking/review-247-9b4edce` returned the full candidate SHA. `gh pr view 247 --json headRefOid,statusCheckRollup` agrees and reports check (22), check (24), rust-lint, rust-test and delivers all SUCCESS. CI run https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/44429730440 is at the same full head; its Rust build/test and lint steps succeeded. No local cargo build or test was run, per the one-build rule. No source was changed.

Owed after merge/deploy: repeat the same exact-counter pair and 20 s machine sampler on the same fleet, recording the new PID/commit, plus daemon CPU/RSS; exercise the planned held-close memory-note scenario. This baseline does not prove a candidate after-deploy improvement. The owner should retain that receipt alongside this verdict. Nonblocking documentation precision: describe grace's process probe as normally in-process with the existing counted fallback, rather than promising no possible launch.
